subproblem.title: Rows of a linear map: |r| <= ||D|| for every row r, and a row family with sum_j |R_j|^2 = |D|^2
subproblem.statement: For all n, l in N and every continuous linear map D : R^n -> R^l: (i) for every j in Fin l and every r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v in R^n, |r| <= ||D|| (operator norm); (ii) there is a family (R_j)_{j in Fin l} in R^n with <R_j, v> = (D v)_j for all j in Fin l and v in R^n, and sum_{j in Fin l} |R_j|^2 = hsNormSq D = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2 (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), (∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (r : Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, inner ℝ r v = D v j) → ‖r‖ ≤ ‖D‖) ∧ ∃ R : Fin ℓ → Rn n, (∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (R j) v = D v j) ∧ ∑ j : Fin ℓ, ‖R j‖ ^ 2 = hsNormSq D
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is step 3 of the parent proof (rows of D = Df(x'), i.e. the gradients grad f^j). The parent uses (i) to get |r| <= ||D|| <= 1 and (ii) to write |D|^2 = sum_j |r_j|^2. No sibling prerequisites; only Mathlib facts about EuclideanSpace are used.

Notation. Fix n, l and D : R^n -> R^l continuous linear. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n (i in Fin n); y_j is the j-th coordinate of y in R^l; <.,.> and |.| are the Euclidean inner product and norm; ||D|| is the operator norm; hsNormSq D = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2.

(i) Row norm bound.
1. Let j in Fin l and r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v. Taking v = r:
 |r|^2 = <r, r> = (D r)_j <= |(D r)_j| <= |D r| <= ||D|| |r|.
 Here |y_j| <= |y| for every y in R^l (PiLp.norm_apply_le) and |D r| <= ||D|| |r| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
2. If |r| = 0, then |r| = 0 <= ||D|| because operator norms are nonnegative. If |r| > 0, dividing |r|^2 <= ||D|| |r| by |r| gives |r| <= ||D||.

(ii) Rows with sum of squares |D|^2.
3. Construction. For j in Fin l, the map v |-> (D v)_j is a continuous linear functional on R^n: the composite (EuclideanSpace.proj j) o D. By the Riesz representation theorem in the finite-dimensional inner product space R^n, R_j := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rn n)).symm ((EuclideanSpace.proj j) o D) satisfies <R_j, v> = (D v)_j for every v (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply). (Equivalently R_j is the vector with coordinates (R_j)_i = (D e_i)_j, and <R_j, v> = sum_i (D e_i)_j v_i = (D (sum_i v_i e_i))_j = (D v)_j.)
4. Coordinates. For every i in Fin n, (R_j)_i = <R_j, e_i> (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right with the scalar 1) = (D e_i)_j by step 3.
5. Parseval. In a Euclidean space |x|^2 is the sum of the squares of the coordinates (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). Hence, by step 4,
 sum_{j in Fin l} |R_j|^2 = sum_{j in Fin l} sum_{i in Fin n} (D e_i)_j^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} sum_{j in Fin l} (D e_i)_j^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2 = hsNormSq D,
 where the middle equality exchanges two finite sums (Finset.sum_comm) and the third applies Parseval in R^l to each D e_i.
6. Steps 3 and 5 give the family R = (R_j)_j required in (ii). For l = 0 or n = 0 the sums are empty and both sides are 0. QED

  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j r hr
    have h1 : ‖r‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖D‖ * ‖r‖ := by

        _ = D r j := hr r
        _ ≤ |D r j| := le_abs_self _
        _ = ‖D r j‖ := (Real.norm_eq_abs _).symm
        _ ≤ ‖D r‖ := PiLp.norm_apply_le (D r) j
        _ ≤ ‖D‖ * ‖r‖ := D.le_opNorm r
    rcases (norm_nonneg r).eq_or_lt with h | h
    · rw [← h]; exact norm_nonneg D
    · nlinarith
  · let R : Fin ℓ → Rn n := fun j => (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rn n)).symm ((EuclideanSpace.proj j).comp D)
    have hR : ∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (R j) v = D v j := by
      intro j v
      simp only [R, InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply]

    refine ⟨R, hR, ?_⟩

    calc ∑ j : Fin ℓ, ‖R j‖ ^ 2 = ∑ j : Fin ℓ, ∑ i : Fin n, (D (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) j) ^ 2 := by
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_)
          rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
          rw [hcoord]
      _ = ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin ℓ, (D (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) j) ^ 2 := Finset.sum_comm
      _ = ∑ i : Fin n, ‖D (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)‖ ^ 2 := by
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
          rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
proof_key_steps: |r|^2 = <r, r> = (D r)_j <= |D r| <= ||D|| |r|, hence |r| <= ||D|| (trivially if r = 0)
R_j := Riesz representative of v |-> (D v)_j, so <R_j, v> = (D v)_j
Parseval twice and exchanging finite sums: sum_j |R_j|^2 = sum_i sum_j (D e_i)_j^2 = sum_i |D e_i|^2 = hsNormSq D

audit.reason: Evaluation at r proves the operator-norm bound with the zero case handled. Riesz representatives provide the rows, and coordinate identities plus exchanged finite sums prove the exact Hilbert–Schmidt identity. No sibling or parent result is assumed.

subproblem.title: Graph orthogonality: p_S e'_j = p_S q(r, 0) when r is the j-th row of D (Simon 4.5 (7))
subproblem.statement: For all n, l in N, every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l), every continuous linear map D : R^n -> R^l, every j in Fin l and every r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v in R^n: let S := span_R{q(graphPoint v (D v)) : v in R^n} and p := S.starProjection. Then p(q(graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))) = p(q(graphPoint r 0)). Here graphPoint a b is the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (j : Fin ℓ) (r : Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, inner ℝ r v = D v j) → (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) = (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint r 0))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is Simon 4.5 (7) ('e_{n+j} - (grad f^j, 0) is normal to the graph'), step 4 of the parent proof. The parent applies it with D = Df(x') and r the j-th row of D. Prerequisite: graph_coords (GA, Submission.any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra): (L2) graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b'; (IP) <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

Notation. Fix n, l, q, D, j and r with <r, v> = (D v)_j for every v in R^n. d_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 in R^l, e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 d_j), g := q(graphPoint r 0), S := span_R{q(graphPoint v (D v)) : v in R^n} and p := S.starProjection (it exists since R^{n+l} is finite-dimensional).

1. The difference. Put x := e'_j - g. Since q is linear, x = q(graphPoint 0 d_j - graphPoint r 0), and by (L2) (read from right to left with a = 0, a' = r, b = d_j, b' = 0), graphPoint 0 d_j - graphPoint r 0 = graphPoint (0 - r) (d_j - 0). So x = q(graphPoint (0 - r) (d_j - 0)) = q(graphPoint (-r) d_j).
2. x is orthogonal to every generator of S. Let v be in R^n. The linear isometry equivalence q preserves inner products (LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map), so by (IP)
 <x, q(graphPoint v (D v))> = <graphPoint (-r) d_j, graphPoint v (D v)> = <-r, v> + <d_j, D v>.
 Here <-r, v> = -<r, v> = -(D v)_j by the hypothesis on r, and <d_j, y> = y_j for every y in R^l (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left with the scalar 1). Hence <x, q(graphPoint v (D v))> = -(D v)_j + (D v)_j = 0.
3. x lies in S-perp. The set of vectors y with <x, y> = 0 is the subspace (R x)-perp (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right). By step 2 it contains every generator q(graphPoint v (D v)), so it contains their span S (Submodule.span_le). Thus <x, y> = 0 for every y in S, i.e. x lies in S-perp (Submodule.mem_orthogonal').
4. Conclusion. The orthogonal projection onto S vanishes exactly on S-perp (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff), so p x = 0. By linearity, 0 = p x = p e'_j - p g, i.e. p(q(graphPoint 0 d_j)) = p(q(graphPoint r 0)). QED

Remark (verified Lean realization; not part of the mathematical argument). Placed inside `namespace Submission` of the Submission file (within namespace GMT.Ch05 with the contract's opens; Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c) as `theorem gwe_gta_graph_row_orthogonal : <frozen type> := by` followed by the body below, it compiled with sorry stubs of the sibling theorem(s) any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra in scope. The same tactic body with the sibling propositions as hypotheses has #print axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
  have hGA := any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra
  intro n ℓ q D j r hr
  have hdiff : q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) - q (graphPoint r 0) =
      q (graphPoint (0 - r) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) - 0)) := by
    rw [← map_sub, (hGA n ℓ).2.2.2.1]
  have hgen : ∀ v : Rn n, inner ℝ (q (graphPoint (0 - r) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) - 0))) (q (graphPoint v (D v))) = 0 := by
    intro v
    rw [LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map, (hGA n ℓ).2.2.2.2.2.2, zero_sub, sub_zero, inner_neg_left,
      hr v, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left]
    simp
  have hmem : q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) - q (graphPoint r 0) ∈
      (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v))))ᗮ := by
    rw [hdiff]
    have hle : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v))) ≤
        (ℝ ∙ q (graphPoint (0 - r) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) - 0)))ᗮ := by
      rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨v, rfl⟩
      exact Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mpr (hgen v)
    refine (Submodule.mem_orthogonal' _ _).mpr (fun u hu => ?_)
    exact Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mp (hle hu)
  have h0 := (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff _).mpr hmem
  rw [map_sub, sub_eq_zero] at h0
  exact h0
proof_key_steps: By linearity of q and (L2), x := q(graphPoint 0 d_j) - q(graphPoint r 0) = q(graphPoint (-r) d_j)
q preserves inner products and (IP) gives <x, q(graphPoint v (D v))> = -<r, v> + (D v)_j = 0 for every v
Orthogonality to all generators gives x in S-perp (span_le into (R x)-perp)
p vanishes on S-perp, so p(q(graphPoint 0 d_j)) = p(q(graphPoint r 0))

audit.reason: The row identity makes q(graphPoint (-r) eps_j) orthogonal to every graph generator. Orthogonality extends to their span, and projection annihilates the difference. This proves the exact equality using only graph_coords.

subproblem.title: Vertical trace identity: sum_j |p_S e'_j|^2 = |p_S - p_T|^2 / 2 for an n-plane S and T = q(R^n x {0}) (Simon 4.4)
subproblem.statement: For all n, l in N, every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l and every linear subspace S of R^(n+l) with finrank S = n: let T := rotatedPlane q = q(R^n x {0}), p := S.starProjection, P := T.starProjection and, for j in Fin l, e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) (the image under q of the standard basis vector with index n + j). Then sum_{j in Fin l} |p e'_j|^2 = hsNormSq(p - P) / 2, where hsNormSq A = sum_{k in Fin (n+l)} |A eps_k|^2 over the standard basis eps_k of R^(n+l), and graphPoint a b is the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), Module.finrank ℝ S = n → ∑ j : Fin ℓ, ‖S.starProjection (q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))))‖ ^ 2 = hsNormSq (S.starProjection - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) / 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is the trace identity of Simon 4.4 in the form used in Simon 4.5 (13): step 6 of the parent proof, for an arbitrary n-dimensional subspace S. The parent applies it to the graph plane S = span{q(graphPoint v (D v)) : v in R^n}, whose dimension n is supplied by the sibling graph_plane_finrank. Prerequisites: - projection_algebra (PA, Submission.hsNorm_starProjection_trace_identities), part (iii): for every m and all subspaces P', T' of R^m with finrank P' = finrank T', trace(T'-perp.starProjection o P'.starProjection) = hsNormSq(P'.starProjection - T'.starProjection) / 2 (LinearMap.trace of the composite of the underlying linear maps). It is applied with m = n + l; Amb n l is by definition Rn (n + l). - graph_coords (GA, Submission.any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra): (C1) (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i; (C2) (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j; (L3) graphPoint (t a) (t b) = t graphPoint a b. - rotated_plane (RP, Submission.any_radius_gr_la_rotatedPlane_facts): (L5) P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0); (L7) finrank (rotatedPlane q) = n. Notation. Fix n, l, q and S with finrank S = n. N := n + l; eps_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 in R^N (k in Fin N); e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n; d_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 in R^l; e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 d_j); T := rotatedPlane q; p := S.starProjection, P := T.starProjection, Q := T-perp.starProjection. All three projections exist since R^N is finite-dimensional. 1. Index facts. Every k in Fin N is castAdd l i for some i in Fin n or natAdd n j for some j in Fin l (Fin.addCases). castAdd l and natAdd n are injective, and castAdd l i' is never natAdd n j', because the values satisfy i' < n <= n + j'. 2. Basis vectors as graph points: eps_{castAdd l i} = graphPoint e_i 0 and eps_{natAdd n j} = graphPoint 0 d_j. Compare coordinates (ext, then the two cases of step 1). The coordinate of eps_k at k' is 1 if k' = k and 0 otherwise (EuclideanSpace.single_apply / PiLp.single_apply). - At castAdd l i': eps_{castAdd l i} has 1 iff i' = i (injectivity); graphPoint e_i 0 has (e_i)_{i'} by (C1), also 1 iff i' = i. eps_{natAdd n j} has 0 there (step 1); graphPoint 0 d_j has 0_{i'} = 0 by (C1). - At natAdd n j': eps_{castAdd l i} has 0 (step 1) and graphPoint e_i 0 has 0_{j'} = 0 by (C2). eps_{natAdd n j} has 1 iff j' = j (injectivity), and graphPoint 0 d_j has (d_j)_{j'} by (C2), also 1 iff j' = j. 3. graphPoint 0 0 = 0 (in R^N): by (L3) with t = 0, a = 0 and b = 0, graphPoint (0 • 0) (0 • 0) = 0 • graphPoint 0 0 = 0, where • is scalar multiplication and 0 • 0 = 0 in R^n and in R^l. 4. Orthonormal basis. b_k := q(eps_k) (k in Fin N) is an orthonormal basis of R^N: it is the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun mapped by the linear isometry equivalence q (OrthonormalBasis.map; (b.map q) k = q(b k)). By step 2, b_{castAdd l i} = q(graphPoint e_i 0) and b_{natAdd n j} = q(graphPoint 0 d_j) = e'_j. 5. Trace in an orthonormal basis. For every linear map L of R^N, trace L = sum_{k in Fin N} . Indeed trace L is the trace of the matrix of L in the basis b (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with b.toBasis), whose (k, k) entry is the k-th coordinate of L b_k, and the k-th coordinate of a vector x in an orthonormal basis is (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply). (Mathlib also states this as LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Trace, which the contract does not import; the matrix route needs no new import.) 6. Apply step 5 to L := Q o p. Since Q is self-adjoint (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right for T-perp), = . Also Q x = x - P x for every x (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val). 7. Horizontal terms vanish. Let y := b_{castAdd l i} = q(graphPoint e_i 0). By (L5) (with a = e_i and second argument 0), P y = q(graphPoint e_i 0) = y. So Q y = y - P y = 0, and = <0, p y> = 0. 8. Vertical terms. By (L5) (with a = 0 and second argument d_j), P e'_j = q(graphPoint 0 0) = q(0) = 0 (step 3 and linearity of q). So Q e'_j = e'_j - 0 = e'_j and the term is . By self-adjointness and idempotence of p (p(p x) = p x since p x lies in S), =

= |p e'_j|^2. 9. Split the sum of step 5 over the two kinds of indices (Fin.sum_univ_add, the bijection of step 1): trace(Q o p) = sum_{i in Fin n} 0 + sum_{j in Fin l} |p e'_j|^2 = sum_{j in Fin l} |p e'_j|^2, by steps 6-8. 10. finrank S = n by hypothesis and finrank T = n by (L7), so finrank S = finrank T. PA(iii) with m = n + l, P' := S and T' := T gives trace(Q o p) = hsNormSq(p - P) / 2. 11. Steps 9 and 10 give sum_{j in Fin l} |p e'_j|^2 = hsNormSq(S.starProjection - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) / 2. All steps hold for n = 0 or l = 0 as well (the corresponding sums are empty).
